items.t: "Fraser VE" is the board/site name for the Fraser sub-area in Vancouver East, City of Vancouver. It is not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas: the Fraser Street corridor runs through four official local areas — Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview — and a block-by-block mapping of the board sub-area to those four areas is UNVERIFIED.

The spine is Fraser Street itself, running south from the East Broadway / Kingsway area to SE Marine Drive, crossed by East Broadway, Kingsway, East King Edward Avenue, East 33rd Avenue, East 41st Avenue, East 49th Avenue and SE Marine Drive.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in small strata buildings on and just off the Fraser Street frontage itself — a 1990s low-rise at 3981 Fraser, a boutique cluster at East 16th–19th Avenues (Vintage Eastside, Mondella, Bold on Fraser, Windsor Views a block east), mid-corridor low-rises at East 41st–49th (Century, Fraserview Court), and one large tower at the south end (Fraser Commons at Marine, 8188 Fraser Street). The side streets are houses with suites and laneway houses under the R1-1 schedule.

Transit: TransLink route 8 Fraser runs Waterfront Station to SE Marine Drive via Fraser Street, Broadway, Kingsway, Main Street and Hastings Street, ending at Fraser Street and East 65th Avenue beside Marine Drive Station (Canada Line); the N8 is the night service on the same corridor. Cross-corridor routes include the 49 at East 49th Avenue, the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, and the 9 at East Broadway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Fraser

items.t: Vancouver zoning: the side streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of the Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m), 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units. The district schedule for the Fraser Street commercial frontage itself: UNVERIFIED in the research pass. The Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview/Killarney community visions and the citywide Vancouver Plan apply along the corridor.

Vancouver tax calendar and Empty Homes Tax: 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date (home owner grant also due July 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraser

items.t: Two of the corridor's biggest "condo" names are rentals. Fraser Commons (747 SE Marine Drive address) and Comma Fraser (Fraser + 19th, 104 rental homes, completed 2023) are purpose-built rental — they dominate search results for the corridor's newest stock while contributing zero strata units.
The City is planning retail growth at Fraser and 33rd.

The library branch has a different name than the corridor. The South Hill Branch of Vancouver Public Library is at 6076 Fraser Street — a buyer searching "Fraser Street library" by corridor name will miss it; it is the branch serving the Sunset stretch of the corridor.

The corridor's hospital is not the famous one. Mount Saint Joseph Hospital sits at the Prince Edward Street entrance beside the corridor in Kensington-Cedar Cottage; Vancouver General Hospital (899 West 12th Avenue) is west of the corridor. Listing copy that assigns VGH to a Fraser address is stretching the geography.

Memorial South Park is the corridor's sports park, and it is not on Fraser. At 5955 Ross Street in Sunset, beside the corridor, with sports fields and courts per the Park Board — the amenity the East 49th–59th stretch of buildings actually uses, under a Ross Street address.

No Fraser-area community centre was confirmed. The research pass could not confirm a City community centre inside the Fraser VE sub-area on a City source — the centres named in sources serve the adjoining local areas. A listing that promises a community centre "in the neighbourhood" for a Fraser address should be checked against the specific centre's address.

Streets, schools and getting around Fraser

items.t: "Fraser VE" is the board / site name for the Fraser sub-area in Vancouver East. Fraser is not one of the City of Vancouver's 22 distinct local areas — the City's areas page lists a smaller area named Fraser, and the Fraser Street corridor runs through four official local areas: Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview. Fraser Street itself is the spine, running south from the East Broadway / Kingsway area to SE Marine Drive.

The City describes Kensington, the southern part of Kensington-Cedar Cottage, as south of Kingsway to 41st Avenue between Fraser and Nanaimo Streets, so Fraser Street forms its west edge there; south of 41st Avenue the corridor passes through Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview toward the Fraser River side of the city. A block-by-block board mapping of the Fraser VE sub-area to the four City local areas: UNVERIFIED.

Transit and roads: route 8 Fraser runs Waterfront Station to SE Marine Drive via Fraser Street, Broadway, Kingsway, Main Street and Hastings Street, with the south end at Fraser Street and East 65th Avenue beside Marine Drive Station (Canada Line); the N8 provides night service on the same corridor; cross-corridor routes include the 49 at East 49th Avenue, the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, and the 9 at East Broadway.

Schools: SD39 catchments are address-based. Schools in the local areas the corridor runs through include Sir Richard McBride Elementary, 1300 East 29th Avenue, and Sir Alexander Mackenzie Elementary, 960 East 39th Avenue, in Kensington-Cedar Cottage, and Henderson Elementary, 451 East 53rd Avenue, Moberly Elementary, 1000 East 59th Avenue, and Trudeau Elementary, 449 East 62nd Avenue, in Sunset.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Fraser

items.t: Fee-simple townhomes and duplexes: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning and Development By-law No. That is the correct frame for the corridor's duplex and laneway product; a "townhouse" listing with no strata fees charged is usually this form, not a strata lot.
Vancouver Empty Homes Tax: A Fraser VE townhouse bought as a secondary or held-vacant property carries this extra annual step.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraser

items.t: "Fraser" is a corridor, not a neighbourhood. The board name Fraser VE spans four official City local areas — Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview — so two homes both sold as "Fraser" can sit in different City planning areas, different community visions and different school catchments.

The library gives the south corridor its other name. The South Hill Branch of Vancouver Public Library is at 6076 Fraser Street — "South Hill" is the local name buyers will hear for the library's part of the corridor.

Memorial South Park is the corridor's big green space, and it is one block off Fraser. At 5955 Ross Street in Sunset, the Park Board lists sports fields and courts — the park buyers picture as "on Fraser" actually fronts Ross Street.

The hospital beside the corridor is not the one buyers assume. Mount Saint Joseph Hospital sits at the Prince Edward Street entrance beside the corridor in Kensington-Cedar Cottage; Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is west of the corridor.

The nearest City community centres named in the sources read serve the adjoining local areas — a buyer who wants a pool or rink programs map should look at the neighbouring areas' centres, not assume one on the corridor.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Fraser
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Side-street house lots: freehold houses on the side streets under the R1-1 District Schedule, many with secondary suites or laneway houses as the schedule permits; strata condos and mixed-use buildings sit on the Fraser Street frontage itself. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees. The split of frontage versus side-street tenure by street is UNVERIFIED.

Lot character: R1-1 minimum site areas run from 306 m² (single detached house, duplex, or 3–4-unit multiple dwelling; minimum frontage 10.0 m) through 464 m² (5 units; 13.4 m) to 557 m² (6–8 units; 15.1 m). These are schedule minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel.

Serviced position: Vancouver homes are on City water and sewer services billed through the City's utility billing; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a Fraser VE house confirmed on a City source is UNVERIFIED. Servicing capacity for a specific multiplex or subdivision proposal is confirmed with the City, parcel by parcel.
ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside the corridor is UNVERIFIED in the research — no ALR parcel is confirmed and no split is stated.

Flood position: the corridor is inland from the Fraser River, but the City's designated floodplain dataset covers the Fraser River coastal floodplain at the south end of the city, and land in the floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for setbacks and flood construction levels. Whether a specific corridor parcel — including the Marine Drive end — is in the floodplain is UNVERIFIED parcel by parcel.

items.t: Nearby areas: Kensington-Cedar Cottage and Riley Park to the north and west, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview along and below the corridor, Knight to the east, Mount Pleasant to the north-west.

Transit: route 8 Fraser runs Waterfront Station to SE Marine Drive via Fraser Street, Broadway, Kingsway, Main Street and Hastings Street, ending at Fraser Street and East 65th Avenue beside Marine Drive Station (Canada Line); the N8 is the night service. Cross-corridor routes include the 49 at East 49th Avenue, the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, and the 9 at East Broadway. There is no SkyTrain station on Fraser Street itself. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: South Hill Branch, Vancouver Public Library, 6076 Fraser Street; Memorial South Park, 5955 Ross Street, in Sunset beside the corridor (sports fields and courts). A Fraser-area community centre confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED. Mount Saint Joseph Hospital sits at the Prince Edward Street entrance beside the corridor; Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is west of the corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Fraser

items.t: Plans: Because "Fraser" is not a local area, the governing vision for a lot is the one for its official local area — confirm which one before relying on any plan claim.

Floodplain standards: land in the City's designated floodplain — which covers the Fraser River coastal floodplain at the city's south end — is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for setbacks and flood construction levels. Check the specific parcel in the City dataset before pricing any south-end lot.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraser

items.t: "Fraser" is four neighbourhoods wearing one street name: because the corridor crosses Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview, two lots both sold as "Fraser" can sit under different City visions, different permit expectations and different school catchments — the board name settles nothing at City Hall.

The corridor's seniors building sits on City-leased land (2023): North Arm Housing Co-operative's 58 homes stand on land the City leases at a nominal rate — the land was never sold, which is why the homes are co-op memberships rather than anything a buyer can acquire.

The library gives the south corridor its other name: the South Hill Branch of Vancouver Public Library is at 6076 Fraser Street — "South Hill" is the local name for the library's stretch of the corridor, and a search under "Fraser library" alone can miss it.

Two of the corridor's biggest new "developments" hold no land a buyer can own: the Fraser Commons rental building (747 SE Marine Drive) and Comma Fraser (104 rental homes, completed 2023) are purpose-built rental on corridor land — they dominate new-stock search results while contributing zero purchasable lots or units.

faq.q: Is Fraser an official City of Vancouver neighbourhood?
faq.a: Not one of the 22 distinct local areas — the City's areas page lists a smaller area named Fraser, and the Fraser Street corridor runs through four official local areas: Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview; "Fraser VE" is the board / site name for the Vancouver East sub-area.

faq.q: Which bus runs the length of Fraser Street?
faq.a: Route 8 Fraser, between Waterfront Station and SE Marine Drive via Fraser Street, Broadway, Kingsway, Main Street and Hastings Street, ending beside Marine Drive Station; the N8 is the night service on the same corridor.

faq.q: Which schools are near the corridor?
faq.a: John Oliver Secondary, 530 East 41st Avenue, is on the corridor, and the VSB directory lists McBride, Mackenzie, Henderson, Moberly and Trudeau elementaries in the adjoining local areas — but catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: When are Vancouver property taxes due in 2026?
faq.a: Advance taxes February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026.
Not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas — the corridor runs through Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Riley Park, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview, and "Fraser VE" is the board name.

faq.q: Is Fraser Commons a condo or a rental?
faq.a: Both names exist at the same development: the 8188 Fraser Street tower (21 storeys, 363 units, built 2021 by Serracan) is strata condo; the 747 SE Marine Drive building marketed as "Fraser Commons Apartments" is purpose-built rental. Check which address a listing actually carries before comparing it to anything.

faq.q: And the building at Fraser and 19th — condo or rental?
faq.a: Also both, on the same corner: Bold on Fraser (688 East 19th Avenue, strata plan EPS4637, 36 units, built 2017) is strata; Comma Fraser is a 104-home purpose-built rental completed 2023. The two are routinely confused in search results.

faq.q: How small are these strata corporations, really?
faq.a: Small: The Sheridan has 11 units and Windsor Views 16, against 363 at Fraser Commons. In an 11-unit strata every owner carries roughly a ninth of any special levy, and a 4-or-fewer-lot depreciation exemption does not apply (all buildings have 5+ units) — read the CRF balance on the Form B with the unit count in mind.

faq.q: Are pets allowed on the corridor?
faq.a: Published examples: The Sheridan and Vintage Eastside listings record "Cats OK"; a Century listing calls the building "pet and transit friendly"; Windsor Views' listing record states pets allowed. Full bylaws (dogs, numbers, size) are UNCONFIRMED from public sources for these buildings — the registered bylaws govern.

faq.q: Are there actually townhouses on the Fraser corridor, or is it all condos and houses?
faq.a: Both exist, but the verified named townhouse stock is four small strata clusters — The Oliver (501 East 44th Avenue, 2017), The Carolina (3918 Carolina Street, 2020), The Saint George (5743 St. George Street, 2014) and Fraser E49 (595 East 49th Avenue, 2026). The corridor's deeper attached supply is apartment condos and its ground-oriented fee-simple supply is duplexes.

faq.q: The listing says "townhouse" but shows no strata fee — what am I buying?
faq.a: Usually a fee-simple duplex or half-duplex on an R1-1 lot: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees, and diligence runs on title and municipal rules instead. Side-street listings in this area expressly market duplexes with "NO STRATA FEES." Check the Title to Land field before assuming either way.

faq.q: Is "The Saint George" the big building near Main Street?
faq.a: No. The Fraser VE complex is the small 2014 strata cluster at 5743 St. George Street; the Mount Pleasant building of the same name at 2471 St. George Street is a different strata in a different sub-area.
